uncertain_or_editorial_candidates.candidate: A compact paired illustration could show the three-state NFA for words whose second symbol from the end is 1, beside its four-state reachable subset DFA. The NFA should have q0 loops on 0 and 1, q0 --1--> q1, and q1 --0,1--> q2 with q2 accepting. The subset states are {q0}, {q0,q1}, {q0,q2}, {q0,q1,q2}; draw transitions by subset update. This would make the claimed four reachable subsets and their distinguishing futures easy to verify. The text already states the construction; absence is not a defect.
checks: Confirm transition set for q0 on 0 is {q0}, on 1 is {q0,q1}; q1 on either symbol reaches q2; q2 has no outgoing NFA transitions.
Only subsets containing q2 accept; use the empty start-word convention consistently (no reachable empty subset).

uncertain_or_editorial_candidates.candidate: A simple directed path sketch u ... z ... v can show the recursive midpoint condition: each half has at most 2^(i-1) edges, so concatenation gives length at most 2^i; conversely split a path at min(2^(i-1), length). This would clarify both directions of the induction. The argument is already complete in prose, so this is optional.
checks: Label midpoint z and both subpaths with upper bound 2^(i-1).
For short paths, place z at the endpoint when length <= 2^(i-1), so the second subpath has length zero.
Keep arrows oriented u through z to v; diagram is explanatory and not a proof substitute.

uncertain_or_editorial_candidates.candidate: A small three-row by four-cell tableau could lay out the exact accepting run and distinguish the marked state/head cell from ordinary symbols; a neighboring local-window inset could show the two transitions and the forbidden changed first successor cell from the refutation. The source gives every row and local tuple explicitly, making the content source-supported. Its absence is not a defect.
checks: Mark the head/state only at row 0 column 0, row 1 column 1, and row 2 column 0; maintain blank guard cell 3.
If showing the counterexample, change only row-1 cell-0 from 0 to 1 and label forbidden tuple (#,a0,B,1); do not confuse the local tuple with the full row.
